rationale: The savepoint selector extends reset comparison from top-level fields to reachable mutable value state.
TemporaryTable.size is a mutable value omitted from the savepoint owner graph.
The oracle closes restored row state against the next admission decision.
The workload mutates value state behind a no-restore container after the checkpoint.
The scenario turns the omitted mutable owner into an observable post-rollback admission decision.
The natural writes place dirty-size mutation strictly after the checkpoint and before rollback.
The schedule carries the RED, control, and exact counterfactual ordering.
Pessimistic lock flags preserve primary membership after savepoint rollback.
The suspicious client-go filter branch has no current TiDB locked temporary-table entry.
No ordinary post-prewrite owner can create the proposed async secondary commitTS split.
The panic-shaped lower path is unreachable through current pipelined DML admission.
